newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close higher, pork bellies sharply up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close higher, pork bellies sharply up.

text.p: CME hogs closed higher, supported by fund buying and strength in both cash hogs and product markets, floor sources said.
They noted the recent run-up in futures prices had turned charts bullish.
"Technically, we are in good shape," one dealer said.
Floor sources said Prudential Securities and E.D. and F. Man International were noted buyers of October hogs with Cargill Investor Services a late seller.
Cash hogs were generally $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher on Monday and seen steady to $0.50 firmer Tuesday.
October hogs closed 0.350 cent higher at 75.925 cents a lb. Dealers said key resistance was located around the 77 cent level. Other months were 0.675 to 0.050 cent higher.

Pork belly futures closed sharply higher with recent light kills helping to tighten supplies. Last week's hog kill was estimated by USDA at 1.586 million, down from 1.616 million a week earlier and 1.629 million in the same week a year ago.

"There is good demand right now and we're tight on supply," said analyst Joe Kropf of Kropf and Love Consulting. He noted there was strong seasonal demand linked to heavy consumption of bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwiches.

Floor sources said Smith Barney and Iowa Grain were early sellers of August pork bellies as positions were downsized as the first month entered the delivery period. The late advance was aided by short covering with Hammer Trading, Prudential Securities and LFG featured.
February bellies were higher for most of the day with Dean Witter, LIT and Refco all featured buyers.
August pork bellies closed up 1.150 cent at 89.150 cents a lb with other months up 1.500 cent to 0.050 cent.
First day deliveries against the August contract are due to be announced early Tuesday.
Floor sources said, however, they did not expect any deliveries to be posted.

Early indications on Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town pork belly storage report were that it would show a net out-movement of around 3.5 million to 3.8 million lbs, slightly higher than last week's net out-movement of 3.467 million.
